chapter: Vidals, blues, teachers and the Silver Leaf band
title: Light-skinned Creole musicians passing for white
summary: They talk of the two Moret brothers, one who could pass, and others such as Matoyi and Mario Bradley.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: The light one didn't pass and the dark one passed. But you couldn't tell him from a nation.
You couldn't tell him from a nation? That's right.
Just like a Mexican, you couldn't tell the difference.
He's had cold, cold black hair and his complexion was, well the same thing with Mario Brad. Mario Brad could pass forever.

I know white people that are proud to have played with on Matoya. He passed. You knew Matoya? No, I know people who played with him. There are plenty of white people who say, oh yeah, I've played with him.
Matoya used to play with him. He played with white too, several times. Oh yeah.
